title: One Place Among Many
angle: A brief change of place can make recovery feel less like fixing oneself and more like rejoining the ordinary world.
paragraphs: There are days when the same room begins to feel like the whole map. The chair, the screen, the familiar patch of window light: nothing is wrong with them, but the world has narrowed to their proportions.

A short walk changes the frame without requiring a destination. At the corner, someone is carrying a loaf in a paper bag; a delivery van blocks half the sidewalk; a tree has dropped small leaves into the gutter. None of this solves whatever was occupying the mind. It does, however, remind attention that other things are happening at once.

That may be one modest shape of recovery: not a dramatic reset, and not proof that a difficult day has been conquered, but a return to the shared scale of ordinary life. Movement can be useful even when it produces no measurable improvement. The route is simply a way of meeting a few details the room could not provide.
Then the door closes behind you, and the same chair is there. It has not become a problem to defeat. It is just one place among many.
